newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 6.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Cronulla rugby league winger Mat Rogers, son of former Australian and New South Wales great Steve Rogers, has altered family footballing allegiances by making himself eligible for Queensland in this year's Super League tri-series. The Sydney-bon winger is making himself eligible to both states under Super League's criteria. Page 4.

In Johannesburg, South Africa, Australian cricketer Shane Warne continued to tighten his hold over South African batsman Daryll Cullinan. Cullinan's tentative first innings and a duck in the second when he attempted to cut Warne late Monday, would have no have healed the scars from his Australian performance three years ago where he averaged five during the three-test series. Monday saw South Africa slide to a 196 run defeat. Page 24.

Australian Queensland rugby union player Tim Horan has been switched from his favoured inside centre position to fullback for the Red's Saturday clash with Northern Transvaal in Pretoria, South Africa. The reshuffle comes as Queensland look for answers to their dismal Super 12 rugby union opener. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian former World No.3 surfer Dave Macaulay is to be fast-tracked into the position of head judge of the world tour surfing competition. Macaulay will replace Brazilian head judge Renato Hickel, starting in mid-April at the World Qualifying series a Margaret River. The promotion has been pushed by leading surfers who have demanded an ex-professional control the subjective judging system. Page 48.

Banned Australian Super League rugby league recruits John Cross and Jack Elsegood have been granted an extra 24-hours to decide which Australian Rugby League Club they wish to play for this season. The pair have until 5pm today to table offers from loyal lubs after the ARL last week won Supreme Court injunctions preventing the pair playing for Super League teams Penrith and Canterbury respectively. Page 47.

Australian Football League team, the Sydney Swans, look likely to appeal to the AFL over a decision to include player Tony McGuiness's contract settlement in this year's salary cap. The Swans may also find themselves reaching their salary cap of $3.2 millon - depending on the settlement size and validity of revision of midfielder Kevin Dyson's contract. Sydney chief executive Kevin Templeton said yesterday the matter would be pursued. Page 47.
THE AGE

New Australian Football League commissioner Craig Kimberley has voiced his weighty support for a second AFL team in Sydney. Speaking for the first time since his election last month, Kimberley said a team to rival the Sydney Swans would be "terrific" and warned the Swans that the days of excessive financial handouts were finished. Page 48.

Australian golfer Greg Norman will not be playing against American 21-year-old Tiger Woods in the US Doral-Ryder Open this week, where the Australian will open his 1997 season. Woods has taken the week off to stay with his father, Earl, who is recovering from bypass surgery. Norman, who has been No.1 in the world ranking longer than anyone else in history, says he will relish the inevitable confrontation. Page B8.

Australian golfer Michelle Ellis has won the Ladies Riversdale Cup, one of the premier events for Australia's amateur women golfers. In her fourth attempt at the tournament, the three-day event was taken out by the 20-year-old Ellis, two shots ahead of 2-year-old Victorian Kate Macintosh. Page 86.
THE HERALD SUN

General manager of Australian Football League team St Kilda Don Hanly said yesterday some clubs had no right to become involved in the Docklands stadium decision, despite the equity involved. He said it was up to teams Hawthorn and the Saints to decide if they wanted to play at the stadium. Hanly said the Saints were as yet undecided over which venue would be better financially. Page 86.

The odds-on favourite for the Qantas Australian Grand Prix and the 1997 world title, Jacques Villeneuve, says he is ready to fight Ferrari's Michael Schumacher and anyone else at the front of the field. After finishing runner-up in his rookie race at Albert Park, Villeneuve only has to improve one place to take the grand prix on Sunday afternoon. Page 88.

The Geelong-Carlton reserves match may only be a March curtain raiser, but may well upstage Saturday night's Ansett Cup clash between the Blues and Freemantle at Waverly Park. After delayed starts to the pre-season, turning out for the twos are such lumiaries as Carlton's Mick McGuane, Greg Williams and Earl Spalding. Geelong's Gary Ablett, Paul Couch and Bill Brownless will also appear after finishing injury lay-offs. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sydney's two weight-for-age race horse giants will come head to head in Monday's $A1.25 million Australian Cup at Flemington, after Juggler's managing owner Peter Horowitz gave his imprimatur for a virtual rematch with Octoganal. Australia's second riches weight-for-age race will be contested after Horowitz passed up Saturday's $300,000 Ranvet Stakes (2000m) at Rosehill in favour of the Australian Cup. Horowitz said the absence of Cox Plate and Melbourne Cup winner Saintly was "one of the factors" influening the decision. Page 82.

German Formula One competitors McLaren boss Ron Dennis and his drivers David Coulthard and Mika Hakkinen yesterday gave the Australian Melbourne Albert Park Grand Prix track the thumbs up yesterday despite rival Michael Schumacher repeating his claims tha it was "nothing special" and not particularly demanding and that the Melbourne track would never see the light of day if it were put forward today. Page 85.

Australian Sydney racetrack experienced high drama yesterday after jockey Larry Cassidy was suspended for five race meetings. Later cleared of the charges, jockey Neil Paine was involved in a complex piece of interference with a lap to travel in the finalevent, Stewards withdrew the charges after fresh evidence. Page 88.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 937-1800
